RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Morgan Lawson
Member ID: W441316160
Reference Number: POC-CBB1679293-79812
Date of Notice: 2026-08-19
Requested Service/CPT Code: Lower back disc surgery / decompression, CPT 63030

Dear Appeal Coordinator:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 63030 (lumbar laminotomy/hemilaminectomy with decompression of nerve root and excision of herniated intervertebral disc) referenced above. The stated reason for denial was that "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." I respectfully disagree, and I am submitting the clinical documentation below to show that this requirement has in fact been met.

Policy Basis for This Appeal

Based on my research, the medical-necessity criteria Aetna applies to lumbar decompression/discectomy procedures such as CPT 63030 are found in Aetna Clinical Policy Bulletin Number 0743, "Spinal Surgery: Laminectomy and Fusion" (https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/700_799/0743.html). I was not able to confirm the effective or last-revised date of the version of CPB 0743 applied to my case, because that information was not visible in the portion of the document I was able to access. I am requesting that the plan identify, in its appeal response, the exact version and date of the medical policy applied to this determination, since I have not independently confirmed that date and am not asserting one.

Subject to that caveat, the retrieved text of CPB 0743 states that Aetna considers the following medically necessary:

"Lumbar laminectomy for individuals with a herniated disc when all of the following criteria are met (see also Additional Notes section): All other reasonable sources of pain and/or neurological deficit have been ruled out, including but not limited to significant pathology at other spinal level(s) on the advanced imaging radiology report that is/are not part of the surgical request resulting in incomplete surgical planning; and Member has signs or symptoms of neural compression (radiculopathy, neurogenic extremity claudication, myelopathy) associated with the levels being treated; and Advanced imaging studies (CT or MRI) indicate central/lateral recess or foraminal stenosis (graded as moderate, moderate to severe or severe; not mild or mild to moderate), or nerve root or spinal cord compression, at the level corresponding with the clinical findings; and Member has failed at least 6 weeks of conservative therapy Footnote1 * (unless there are indications for waiver of requirements for conservative management, noted below); and Member's activities of daily living are limited by symptoms of neural compression."

I was not able to retrieve the specific text of "Footnote1" defining "conservative therapy" for this policy from the source document, so I do not quote or assume its contents here. I address conservative treatment below using the general categories referenced elsewhere in the policy excerpt I did retrieve (physical therapy, medications, and injections), and I ask the plan to confirm whether any additional or different elements were required.

How the Clinical Record Meets Each Criterion

1. Imaging-confirmed compression at the level corresponding to clinical findings:
MRI of the lumbar spine dated 2026-06-23 documents an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root. This is a severe-grade finding at the level directly implicated by the physical examination and symptoms described below, which — based on the policy language quoted above — corresponds to the imaging severity threshold ("moderate, moderate to severe or severe; not mild or mild to moderate") described in CPB 0743.

2. Signs or symptoms of neural compression:
The clinical record documents radicular pain radiating into the right calf and a neurologic deficit on examination corresponding to the imaged L4-L5 level, along with positive provocative testing on the affected side. These findings correspond to the "signs or symptoms of neural compression (radiculopathy...)" element quoted above.

3. At least 6 weeks of conservative therapy:
The record documents substantially more than 6 weeks of conservative management, including:
   - 18 months of progressive low back pain unrelieved by rest;
   - Supervised physical therapy, including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility training, over 12 weeks (2026-04-13 through 2026-07-06), with 16 visits completed, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note;
   - NSAID therapy for 8 months with inadequate relief;
   - A corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-25, which produced only 4 weeks of partial relief.
This combination of therapy modalities and duration substantially exceeds the 6-week conservative-therapy period referenced in the quoted policy language.

4. Activities of daily living limited by symptoms of neural compression:
The record documents that the patient cannot stand for more than 10 minutes at a time, which is a direct, functionally significant limitation attributable to the L4-L5 nerve root compression and radicular symptoms described above.

5. Other reasonable sources of pain ruled out:
The record notes no active infection and no untreated substance use, and the imaging and exam findings localize the pathology to the L4-L5 level, with no indication of competing pathology at another spinal level.

Requested Action

Based on the above, I ask Aetna to reverse the denial and approve CPT 63030 as requested by Dr. Duval. If the plan believes any specific element of its medical policy (including the contents of "Footnote1" or any other criterion I was unable to retrieve) has not been met, I ask that the plan state that specific unmet criterion in writing, quote the exact policy language relied upon, and identify the policy version/date, so that I and my surgeon can respond directly.

Additional Matters for Clarification

I also note that this notice identifies my plan as "Aetna Better Health of West Virginia (Commercial/ACA)" and states an appeal deadline of 180 days (by 2027-02-15). Publicly available Aetna Better Health of West Virginia materials describe this entity as a Medicaid/WVCHIP managed-care plan with a standard appeal window of 60 calendar days from the date of the denial notice. Because of this discrepancy, I am filing this appeal well within 60 days of the notice date out of caution, and I ask the plan to confirm in writing (a) which specific plan type/product governs my coverage, and (b) the appeal and, if applicable, external review or state fair hearing deadlines that actually apply to my case.

- Medication records showing 8 months of NSAID therapy
- Record of corticosteroid injection dated 2026-05-25 and documented response

Sincerely,

Morgan Lawson
